Class MKCMenu

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.screen.MKCMenu
public final class MKCMenu extends Object
The turnkey custom-menu primitive — one define(...).register() chain replaces the ~4 plumbing pieces a consumer used to hand-write for every custom MKCScreenHandler menu (its own MenuType registration, its own open C2S payload + receiver, its own MenuScreens.register, its own open call). Modeled on MKCContainerPanel.define(...).register().

Recipe

// Consumer COMMON initializer (runs both sides):
public static final MKCMenu CUSTOM = MKCMenu
    .define(Identifier.fromNamespaceAndPath(MOD_ID, "custom_menu"), MyMenu::buildHandler)
    .title(Component.literal("My Custom Menu"))   // optional; default = "menu.<ns>.<path>"
    .screen(MyScreen::new)                         // optional; default MKCHandledScreen::new
    .arm(MyMenu::armBehaviors)                     // optional; arm slot behavior by Address, same chain
    .register();

// The handler factory receives the menu's own MenuType (no reach-back to the
// CUSTOM handle being assigned above — see HandlerFactory):
public static MKCScreenHandler buildHandler(
        MenuType<MKCScreenHandler> type, int syncId, Inventory inv) {
    return MKCScreenHandler.builder(type)        // type handed in, never CUSTOM.getType()
            .panel("mymod:menu:main", p -> p.group("items", storage))
            .build(syncId);
}

// Open it:
CUSTOM.requestOpen();        // client → sends the one generic open payload
CUSTOM.open(serverPlayer);   // server-side direct (no networking)

Why the factory takes the MenuType

A handler must call MKCScreenHandler.builder(MenuType) with this menu's MenuType, but that type is built inside register(). If the factory had to reach back to the static handle the define(...).register() chain is still mid-assigning (e.g. CUSTOM.getType()), it would work only because the factory runs lazily — a consumer who evaluates the type eagerly or inlines the define call hits a forward-reference / null trap. So the factory is a MKCMenu.HandlerFactory that is handed the freshly-built type: both the MenuType's own client-side factory lambda and the server-side SimpleMenuProvider in open(ServerPlayer) pass type in. The consumer never names the handle.

The client/server split

register() is side-neutral (common init): it builds + registers the MenuType, stores the title + screen factory + id on the returned handle, and adds the handle to DEFINITIONS (so the client can drain it) + the id-keyed BY_ID map (so the generic server receiver can resolve it). The screen factory is a MKCMenuScreenFactory — a never-server-invoked functional interface, materialised into a vanilla screen only on the client from registerScreens() (same discipline as MKCContainerPanel.chrome).

Namespace your panel ids

This menu's getId() Identifier is globally unique, but it does NOT scope the Addresses of the slots the menu's handler creates — those are keyed globally by (panelId, groupId, localIndex) (see CreatedSlotAdapter.addressOf). So the panel ids the handler declares (via MKCScreenHandler.builder(MenuType)) must be namespaced per-mod — e.g. "mymod:menu:main" — exactly as container-parity panel ids already are, or two mods that both name a panel "main" will collide and arm each other's slots. That id is the same one used for layout references and for addressing in MKCMenu.Builder.arm.

  • Method Details

    • define

      public static MKCMenu.Builder define(net.minecraft.resources.Identifier id, MKCMenu.HandlerFactory handlerFactory)
      Begins a custom-menu definition.
      Parameters:
      id - the registry id for the menu's MenuType (also the key the generic open payload carries)
      handlerFactory - builds the MKCScreenHandler from (type, syncId, playerInventory) — handed the menu's own MenuType so it never reaches back to the handle being assigned; runs identically on both sides (server via the menu provider, client via the MenuType factory), so storages must be same-size for sync

    • getType

      public net.minecraft.world.inventory.MenuType<MKCScreenHandler> getType()
      This menu's registered MenuType.

    • getId

      public net.minecraft.resources.Identifier getId()
      This menu's registry id (also the open-payload key).

    • open

      public void open(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player)
      Opens this menu for the given server player — server-side direct, no networking. Vanilla syncs the open to the client, which rebuilds the menu through this menu's MenuType and shows the registered screen.

    • requestOpen

      public void requestOpen()
      Requests the server open this menu for the local player — client-side. Sends the one library-owned generic open payload carrying this menu's id; the server receiver (registered in MKC.init()) resolves the handle and calls open(ServerPlayer) on the main thread.

    • byId

      @Internal public static MKCMenu byId(net.minecraft.resources.Identifier id)
      Resolves a menu by the id carried in an open payload, or null if no menu was registered under that id. The generic server receiver in MKC.init() uses this — an unknown id is a fail-loud log, never an NPE.

    • registerScreens

      @Internal public static void registerScreens()
      Registers every defined menu's screen with MenuScreens. Client-only — invoked once from MKCClient.onInitializeClient, after all consumer common-init register() calls have populated DEFINITIONS (Fabric runs all main entrypoints before any client entrypoint). The screen factory is materialised into a vanilla ScreenConstructor only here.
